resources.string: Leave empty for the whole document

One file per top-level entry in the document\'s own table of contents, which is the natural way to break up a scanned book or a bundle of statements. Documents without one say so rather than guessing.
One PDF, a page per image

Paragraphs, headings, lists and tables, with Word\'s own styles, so the navigation pane works and the text reflows when edited. A PDF holds lines, not paragraphs, so this is reconstruction: check a long document after.
One sheet per page. Lines that line up in columns become cells; a number stays a number so sums work. Best on statements and tables.
A reflowing book for e-readers, cut into chapters at the headings.
One self-contained web page, pictures included, that opens in any browser.
One slide per page, in the page\'s own shape: a picture of each page, exactly as it looks, or its lines as text boxes you can edit.
Scanned pages have no words until Make searchable has read them.

Paragraphs, headings, lists and tables come through, laid out on A4 in the phone\'s own fonts - Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam and the rest included, where the phone has the font. Shapes, text boxes and tracked changes do not.
The levels are tried lightest first and the first that fits is kept. If none fits, you get the smallest and are told; Split by size can then cut it into parts that do.
Let pages become pictures if that is what it takes
Only when no level gets under the size. Each page becomes one picture that looks the same; its words are kept underneath, so search and copy still work.
Sheaf shrinks the images inside a document and leaves text untouched, so text stays sharp and selectable. A document with no scanned pages will barely change.
That could not be measured. Running it will still tell you.
%1$s - already as small as it goes at this level, so the original would be kept.
Sheaf encrypts with AES-256 and does not keep the password anywhere. If you forget it, the document cannot be opened again - not by us either.
The file opens without a password. It is encrypted with a key nobody is given, so the restrictions below cannot be lifted by typing one.
These three are a request, not a lock. The PDF standard asks readers to honour them and most do, but a reader that ignores them can. Anyone who can open the file can print it to a new one.
These three are a request, not a lock. The PDF standard asks readers to honour them and most do, but a reader that ignores them can. The encryption is the part that actually holds.
Files are joined top to bottom. Use the arrows to reorder them.
You need the document\'s password. Sheaf opens it the way any reader would and saves an unlocked copy - it cannot recover a password you do not have.

Sheaf reads the words in a scan and lays them invisibly over the page, so the document looks exactly the same but you can search, select and copy it. Both models are inside the app; nothing is downloaded. This is the slowest tool here - expect around a second a page - and it keeps running if you switch to another app.
Whatever the form asks for, at least 2 KB.
As many pixels as it has, unless it needs fewer to fit.
413 × 531 pixels (300 dpi), cut from the middle to that shape.
Cut from the middle to that shape, then made exactly that size.

Each picture comes out as a JPEG under the size you choose, as sharp as that allows. Here 1 KB is 1,000 bytes, so it is under the limit however the form counts. The phone\'s hidden details, its location too, are left out.

The old words are painted over in the page\'s own colour and the new ones written in their place: in the document\'s own font where it can be, otherwise the nearest built-in one, and squeezed a little to stay inside a table cell. Hindi, Malayalam and every other script the phone shows can be typed. On a scan, only the words you change are repainted. The old words stay inside the file underneath, so anyone who copies the text can still find them: to take words out for good, use Remove areas.
The next box you drag becomes a
Drag a box on the page above where each field should go, then name it in the list. The result is a real PDF form: anyone can fill it in, in any reader, and Fill in a form here seals the answers.

Pick the PDF, then your certificate: a .pfx or .p12 from your bank, your employer or a signing service. The signature is the kind every reader\'s panel checks. The certificate and its password are used for this run and kept nowhere. This is not the same as Sign, which draws a picture of a signature.

PDF/A-2b is what records offices, courts and auditors ask for: a file that will open the same way in twenty years. The copy gets a colour profile, archive details and no scripts, attachments or password. A font the file uses but does not carry is the one thing that cannot be fixed here, and the result says if so.

Add the older version first and the newer one second. The newer one comes back marked: new words highlighted in green, and a note wherever words were taken out saying what they were. Words only - a changed picture or layout is not seen.
Owner\'s PAN (needed over Rs. 1 lakh a year)

One receipt a month, two to a page, with the amount in words as a receipt writes it. Print, get them signed by the owner, and hand them in with your HRA claim. Nothing typed here is kept or sent anywhere.
Sized to the page, so DRAFT and CONFIDENTIAL both cross it; longer text is shrunk to fit.
One unbroken run across every file given, in the order they are listed: the second file carries on from where the first ended.
Each page is trimmed to just outside its words and pictures, with 2 mm of white kept. A page with nothing to find is left alone.
Measured on the page as you read it, whichever way it is stored.
Scale small pages up to fit
Keep small pages their real size
Cropping hides the margins rather than deleting them, which is how every PDF reader works. To take something out of a page for good, use Remove areas.

Drawn behind what is already on the page, so the text stays on top. A scanned page is one solid picture, so a colour will not show through it. Dark leaves black type unreadable; it is for pages of white type or pictures.
Readers go back to counting from the first page.

Labels change what a reader shows in its page box, not what is printed on the page. A report whose page 1 is the ninth sheet is the reason: with labels, typing 57 goes to 57. For numbers on the page itself, use Page numbers.
Bookmarks are the table of contents a reader shows in its side panel. Edit the list above: a title and the page it opens. Indent an entry to nest it under the one before.
Every file inside the document comes out as its own result, as it was.
The first file is the PDF. Everything added after it is carried inside the copy byte for byte and never opened - a spreadsheet, a photo, another PDF. Readers list them in their attachments panel.
This draws your signature into the page, the same as printing, signing and scanning it back. It is not a cryptographic digital signature.
Width, as a share of the page
Pick the PDF, then the image: PNG, JPEG or WebP. It is drawn into the page, so the next reader cannot drag it off.

Tap the page below to choose where the text goes. Covering paints white over the old text rather than deleting it, so it is a correction, not a redaction - use Remove areas when something has to be gone for good.

Four things are filled in as each page is stamped: {page} the page number, {total} how many there are, {date} today, and {name} the document\'s name. \"Confidential - {date}\" works, so does \"{name} - page {page} of {total}\".
The first file is the document being added to. Add a second file and its pages go in; add nothing and you get blank pages instead.
Blank pages, if no second file
The new pages go in where the first of these was
Tap the page where it should go.
Marks are drawn into the page rather than added as notes, so they are still there in any other reader - and cannot be peeled off again. The document you chose is never changed either way.
Sealing draws the answers into the page and removes the fields, so nobody can retype them. It cannot be undone, and the editable original is untouched - Sheaf never writes to the file you chose.
The result stays a form, so the answers can be changed later by anyone who opens it.
The sheet is turned whichever way shows the pages biggest: two upright pages side by side on a sideways sheet, two wide slides one above the other.
Each part is measured by saving it, so none comes out over the limit - except a single page that is bigger than the limit on its own, which becomes its own part and is marked.
Clears the title, author, subject, keywords, the app that made it and the dates. A scanner writes its make and model into a PDF; a word processor writes the name it is licensed to.
Takes out what a file gives away before it is sent: the details and their hidden XMP copy, page thumbnails and private editing data, and whichever of these you choose. The result says what was found.

For all %1$d files: a box you fill is set on every one; a box left empty keeps each file\'s own.

resources.string: These are the document\'s current details. Edit whichever you want to change; an empty box clears it.
This pulls out the pictures already inside the document at their original size. For pictures of the pages themselves, use PDF to images.

Draw a box over anything that should go. The marked pages are rebuilt as images, so what was underneath is genuinely gone rather than covered - and those pages stop being selectable text. Other pages are untouched.

Picks the sentences that carry the document, and lists the amounts, dates and percentages in it. Every point is a sentence from the document itself, so each can be found again in the original. Worked out on this phone; nothing is sent anywhere. A scan needs Make searchable first. Translation needs a language model this app does not download, so it is not offered.
